title: Smooth atlas comparison and arbitrary base change for algebraic stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use the fibred groupoids, morphisms, representability and 2-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], with algebraic spaces as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A morphism $p:W\to\mathcal X$ from a scheme is representable smooth if every scheme base change is an algebraic space whose projection to the base is smooth on every etale scheme chart [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; surjective means surjective on field-valued point classes after scheme base change. Then $\mathcal X$ is smooth over $S$ in the atlas sense of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] if and only if, for every scheme $W$ and representable smooth $p:W\to\mathcal X$, the composite $W\to S$ is smooth. No surjectivity of $p$ is assumed in this test. For every scheme morphism $S'\to S$, the 2-fibre product $\mathcal X_{S'}=\mathcal X\times_S S'$ is algebraic, and the base change of any smooth surjective scheme atlas of $\mathcal X$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas of $\mathcal X_{S'}$. If $\mathcal X$ is smooth over $S$, then $\mathcal X_{S'}$ is smooth over $S'$. No finite-type, Noetherian or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis on $\mathcal X$ or $S$ is imposed.

proof.text: Assume that $\mathcal X$ is smooth over $S$, and choose a smooth surjective atlas $a:U\to\mathcal X$ with $U\to S$ smooth, as in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. For an arbitrary representable smooth $p:W\to\mathcal X$, put $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}W$. By representability, $R$ is an algebraic space. The representable-map calculus [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus] says that $R\to U$ is smooth and $q:R\to W$ is smooth and surjective. Regard the schemes as their representable algebraic spaces [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-smooth-source-point-locality] first to $R\to U\to S$: since $U\to S$ is smooth everywhere, $R\to S$ is smooth everywhere. For each point $w$ of $W$, choose a point $r$ of $R$ over $w$, using surjectivity of $q$. Apply that same pointwise equivalence to $R\xrightarrow{q}W\to S$ at $r$: smoothness of $R\to S$ at $r$ gives smoothness of $W\to S$ at $w$. Smoothness on neighbourhoods of every point is smoothness of the morphism. This proves the forward implication without assuming $p$ surjective.

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target), proof of (2) implies (1), specialized to target S; spaces-descent.tex Tag 06F2 (lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source)

proof.text: Conversely, algebraicity supplies a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:U\to\mathcal X$ by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Apply the assumed test to this particular representable smooth map. It gives $U\to S$ smooth, so this atlas witnesses smoothness of $\mathcal X$ over $S$ by the definition.

Let $S'\to S$ be arbitrary. The schemes $S$ and $S'$ are algebraic stacks over $S$ through their representable sheaves [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]: a representable sheaf is an fppf, hence etale, sheaf, so a stack with discrete fibres; its diagonal is represented by scheme fibre products; and its identity is a scheme atlas whose scheme base changes are identities, hence smooth and surjective. The algebraic-stack fibre-product theorem [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], applied over $S$ to $\mathcal X\to S\leftarrow S'$, gives the algebraic stack $\mathcal X'=\mathcal X\times_S S'$. Interpreting it over $S'$ uses [lem-sfb-etale-stack-localization]: objects and etale descent over an $S'$-scheme are the same objects and descent data with the specified map to $S'$. The diagonal tests are unchanged: for two objects over $T\to S'$, their isomorphism sheaf is the same algebraic space as before. For any smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$, the scheme fibre product $U'=U\times_S S'$ exists by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The triples describing the 2-fibre products in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] identify $U'$ with $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X'$: the extra object of $\mathcal X$ is identified with the image of the object from $U$, leaving precisely its map to $S'$ and the equality of the maps to $S$. Hence $U'\to\mathcal X'$ is the 2-base change of the original atlas, so [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus] makes it representable smooth and surjective. This gives the required atlas over $S'$, and together with the stack and diagonal tests verifies algebraicity over $S'$.

source.place: algebraic.tex Tag 04T2 (lemma-2-fibre-product), Tags 0302 and 045C (base change of representability and representable properties); stacks.tex Tag 04WV (lemma-localize-stacks)

proof.text: If $\mathcal X$ is smooth over $S$, choose its atlas $U$ with $U\to S$ smooth [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. For this atlas, the structural morphism $f':U'=U\times_S S'\to S'$ is the scheme base change of $f:U\to S$ along $S'\to S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. A smooth morphism of schemes is flat and locally of finite presentation [lem-pc-smooth-flat], so the pointwise base-change lemma [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] applies to $f$ and the arbitrary morphism $S'\to S$: for every $u'\in U'$, $f'$ is smooth at $u'$ because $f$ is smooth at the image of $u'$ in $U$. Smoothness on an open neighbourhood of every point is smoothness of $f'$, since these open neighbourhoods cover $U'$ and smoothness of schemes is local on the source. Thus $U'\to S'$ is smooth. The atlas $U'\to\mathcal X'$ established in the preceding step therefore witnesses smoothness of $\mathcal X'$ over $S'$ by the definition [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. This argument places no flatness, finiteness or Noetherian restriction on the base-changing map.
